title: What this knowledge body deliberately does NOT hold, and what to do instead
content:
Read this before answering any security question that turns on a specific published vulnerability, and before writing any sentence containing a version number.

THIS BODY HOLDS NO ADVISORY IDENTIFIER. No vulnerability identifier, no security advisory reference, no severity score. It holds no claim that any particular version of any component is vulnerable, unpatched, or fixed. And it holds no assertion about what version of anything this estate is currently running.

WHY, stated as a reason rather than as caution. The session that authored this body could not read a vulnerability feed and cannot re-read one later. A statement of that kind, written here, would have been invented at the moment of writing and would then decay whether or not it started true. A stale security claim is worse than no claim, because it carries a specific number and gets acted on with confidence, and nothing in a knowledge body announces its own expiry.

HOW IT IS ENFORCED RATHER THAN PROMISED. Six banned shapes are scanned by the loader across every record, authored and generated alike, and one hit aborts the entire run before anything is written. The evaluation runs those same patterns against strings deliberately carrying each shape and requires all six to fire, because a guard that has refused nothing has not been shown to work.

WHAT IS NOT BANNED: the words, and the concepts. A record describing how to determine whether a published advisory reaches this estate is exactly what this seat needs and is present. The identifier is banned; the noun is not.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, when the question genuinely needs a specific. Read the version from the running platform, never from a record. Read the advisory from its own publisher. And when the estate's own dated threat snapshot is consulted -- it exists, elsewhere, and names specifics -- treat it exactly as its own first record instructs: as a point-in-time picture whose durable value is the CLASS of vulnerability, never as a current position.

And the rule for this seat's own output: an identifier that did not come from a source read in the same session is invented. There is no third possibility, and no amount of confidence changes that.

holds_none_of: a claim that a version is vulnerable, unpatched or fixed
an assertion about what version this estate runs
structured_data.reason: the authoring session could not read a vulnerability feed and cannot re-read one; such a statement would be invented at writing and decay afterwards, and a stale security claim carries a specific number and is acted on with confidence
structured_data.enforcement: six banned shapes scanned by the loader over every record, authored and generated; one hit aborts the run before any write; the evaluation proves all six fire against deliberately bad strings
structured_data.not_banned: the words and the concepts -- how to determine whether an advisory reaches this estate is present
do_instead: read the version from the running platform, never from a record
read the advisory from its own publisher
treat the estate's dated threat snapshot as its own first record instructs -- a point-in-time picture whose durable value is the class
structured_data.output_rule: an identifier not from a source read this session is invented; there is no third possibility

title: This body is not a certification, and live state is never stored here
content:
Two further limits, both of which prevent a specific kind of confident error.

THIS IS NOT A SECURITY CERTIFICATION. It is authored engineering method, diagnostic lenses this codebase has paid for, measured facts about this estate, and security operations grounded here. It does not confer, claim or imply any professional accreditation, and no answer drawn from it should be presented as one. The reason for saying so INSIDE the corpus rather than only in a comment is that an agent retrieving from here should be told its limits by the thing it is reading, not by documentation it will never see.

LIVE STATE IS NOT STORED HERE. What is failing right now, what a log currently says, which deploy is current, how many rows a table holds today, whether a job ran this morning -- none of that belongs in a knowledge record, because it would be wrong within hours and would then be quoted with the same confidence as something durable. Where a record needs such a fact, it names the query, the log or the endpoint that holds it rather than holding a snapshot.

THE FIVE GENERATED RECORDS ARE THE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION and each says so on its face. They are built by the loader from live rows at load time -- the scheduler baseline, the privileged-routine surface, the row-security posture, the corpus inventory and this seat's own model pair with its prices. Nothing in them is hand-typed, which is the structural guarantee that they cannot contradict the system, and each states that it describes the position as at the load run and names the query that refreshes it. If a generated record disagrees with a measurement you just took, the measurement is right and the record is stale, and the repair is to re-run the loader rather than to edit a number.

The general principle behind both limits: a knowledge body should hold what stays true, name where the rest lives, and never quietly hold a third thing that used to be true.

structured_data.limit_one: not a security certification; it confers and implies no accreditation, and this is stated inside the corpus so a retrieving agent is told its limits by what it reads
structured_data.limit_two: live state is not stored -- what is failing now, current logs, the current deploy, today's row counts, this morning's job run
structured_data.instead: name the query, log or endpoint that holds it
structured_data.deliberate_exception: five loader-generated records -- the scheduler baseline, the privileged-routine surface, the row-security posture, the corpus inventory, and this seat's model pair with prices
structured_data.why_generated: nothing hand-typed, so they cannot contradict the system; each states it describes the load-run position and names its refresh query
structured_data.on_disagreement: a fresh measurement wins over a generated record; re-run the loader rather than edit a number
structured_data.principle: hold what stays true, name where the rest lives, never quietly hold a third thing that used to be true

title: The one standing hold, and the instruction not to raise it
content:
There is exactly one standing limit on this estate's engineering: paid model routes are held closed. A gate refuses every paid provider call, and it is in force.

WHAT THAT MEANS OPERATIONALLY, because the consequences are frequently misread.

A deterministic path taken instead of a model call is CORRECT BEHAVIOUR under the hold, not a degradation and not an incident. The comparison engine's model-free fallback is the expected path today. A report produced that way is a working system, and escalating it as a quality problem misdiagnoses a design decision as a fault.

Registering a model pair is a routing declaration, not a call. Pinning which models a seat WOULD use costs nothing while the hold is on and is what makes the routing correct on the day it lifts. There is no contradiction between the hold being in force and a pair being registered.

Embedding is NOT affected and this matters, because it is what makes knowledge bodies work at all. The embedding path runs in-region on a small local model and short-circuits before any routing or budget decision, so it is free and reaches no paid provider. Anything that needs a vector gets one.

AND THE INSTRUCTION, which is about conduct rather than engineering: do not raise the hold with the founder. It is settled, it stays until the whole build is finished, and it has been re-litigated enough times that raising it again wastes his time. Deterministic-first is the architecture here, not a workaround for a temporary condition -- the system is being built so that the routine work happens without a model at all, and the reasoning layer adds judgement on top when it is on.

So when a capability appears blocked on inference, the correct move is to build the deterministic version and ship it, not to note the blocker and stop. A blocker is a claim too, and this particular one has an answer that does not require anybody's permission.

structured_data.the_one_limit: paid model routes are held closed and a gate refuses every paid provider call
consequences: a deterministic path instead of a model call is correct behaviour, not a degradation or an incident
registering a model pair is a routing declaration, not a call, and costs nothing while the hold is on
embedding is unaffected -- it runs in-region on a small local model and short-circuits before routing and budget, so it is free and reaches no paid provider
structured_data.conduct_instruction: do not raise the hold with the founder; it is settled, stays until the build is finished, and has been re-litigated enough times
structured_data.architecture: deterministic-first is the design, not a workaround -- routine work happens without a model, and reasoning adds judgement on top when it is on
structured_data.when_something_looks_blocked_on_inferenc: build the deterministic version and ship it; do not note the blocker and stop

title: There are no phase gates, no freezes and no kernel gates: do not reinstate one
content:
A large amount of machinery that used to constrain changes in this estate has been removed on the founder's explicit instruction, and an IT seat will keep encountering its residue. Knowing it is gone -- and gone deliberately -- prevents two errors: treating a leftover reference as corruption, and helpfully rebuilding something that was removed on purpose.

WHAT IS GONE. Every phase freeze and phase gate. The baseline drift boards and the statement guards that enforced them. The organisation chart, departments, workflows, handoffs, subscriptions and executors. The kernel write and trace gates. Thirteen checks were RETIRED -- not weakened -- because every noun they asserted had been deliberately deleted, and each is preserved with a header saying what it checked and why it is gone, specifically so nobody resurrects one.

IN HIS WORDS, the reasoning was that the phases were scaffolding for getting the structure right, that their freezes and implied limits should be removed totally, and that the only thing on hold is the paid-route gate -- because otherwise the code would never be finished.

SO: do not write a check that asserts a baseline is unchanged. Do not re-attach a kernel gate. Do not rebuild a workflow registry or write a department into anything. A structure that cannot move cannot be corrected, and the live system has moved past those registers.

WHAT SURVIVED, AND IS NOT STRUCTURE. Correctness and security guards, all of which stay: constraints, foreign keys, the authority guard that asks for a change reason, credential tests, the verification-setting drift check, the protection against wholesale table truncation, and the check that the anonymous role cannot execute a privileged routine. Append-only protection on history tables also stays -- it stops history being rewritten and refuses no change.

The distinction to carry: a guard that protects CORRECTNESS stays; a gate that protected a STRUCTURE is gone with the structure. When the new structure exists, new checks get written against that, not resurrected from this.

removed: every phase freeze and phase gate
baseline drift boards and their statement guards
the organisation chart, departments, workflows, handoffs, subscriptions, executors
thirteen checks, RETIRED not weakened, each preserved with a header saying what it checked and why it is gone
structured_data.reasoning: the phases were scaffolding for getting the structure right; their freezes and implied limits were removed totally, leaving the paid-route gate as the only hold, because otherwise the code would never be finished
do_not: write a check asserting a baseline is unchanged
survived: the authority guard requiring a change reason
the anonymous-role cannot execute a privileged routine check
structured_data.distinction: a guard protecting correctness stays; a gate protecting a structure went with the structure
